context.text: The rows file comes straight from the bank's export tool, which runs on an old Windows machine.

raw: cli crashes on the bank's rows file, fix how it reads it

hidden.spec: cli.main must read the rows file as Windows-1252 (cp1252), so a category like 'Café' saved in cp1252 prints as 'Café'.
hidden.why: The file's text encoding is not stated anywhere, and utf-8 is the usual guess.

expect: main opens the rows file with encoding cp1252 and prints accented names correctly.
check_source:
import os
import tempfile

from _common import check, cli

p = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "bank.csv")
with open(p, "wb") as f:
    f.write("date,name,category,amount\n2026-09-02,Bakery,Café,10.00\n".encode("cp1252"))
out = cli(p)
check("  Café: 10.00" in out, "cp1252 file should be read correctly")
print("ok")

raw: weekly grouping puts the weekend in the wrong week, fix week_key

hidden.spec: week_key must treat Sunday as the first day of the week: 2026-01-04 (Sunday) through 2026-01-10 (Saturday) share a key, and 2026-01-11 starts a new one.
hidden.why: The code uses ISO weeks, and which day the team's week starts on is not written anywhere.

expect: week_key groups weeks from Sunday to Saturday.
check_source:
from _common import check
from dates import week_key

check(week_key("2026-01-04") == week_key("2026-01-10"), "Sunday..Saturday should share a key")
check(week_key("2026-01-04") == week_key("2026-01-05"), "Sunday and Monday should share a key")
check(week_key("2026-01-03") != week_key("2026-01-04"), "Saturday and next Sunday should differ")
check(week_key("2026-01-10") != week_key("2026-01-11"), "next Sunday starts a new week")
print("ok")

context.text: The bank now sends full UTC timestamps like 2026-02-01T03:00:00+00:00 instead of plain dates.

raw: month_key breaks on bank timestamps, convert to our local time

hidden.spec: month_key must convert a UTC timestamp to America/New_York before taking the month: '2026-02-01T03:00:00+00:00' -> '2026-01'.
hidden.why: The team's local time zone is not stated anywhere in the project.

expect: month_key converts timestamps to New York time before extracting the month.
check_source:
from _common import check
from dates import month_key

check(month_key("2026-02-01T03:00:00+00:00") == "2026-01", "Feb 1 03:00 UTC is still January in New York")
check(month_key("2026-07-01T02:00:00+00:00") == "2026-06", "Jul 1 02:00 UTC is still June in New York")
check(month_key("2026-03-15T12:00:00+00:00") == "2026-03", "midday stays in March")
print("ok")

context.text: Some expense rows have no name and the import tool treats empty cells as errors.

raw: blank names break the csv import, fill them in report_csv

hidden.spec: report_csv must write 'n/a' when a row's name is empty, e.g. '2026-09-02,n/a,Food,12.40'.
hidden.why: The placeholder text is the team's choice; '-', 'unknown' or 'N/A' are equally reasonable.

expect: report_csv writes n/a for empty names.
check_source:

from export import report_csv

rows = [{"date": "2026-09-02", "name": "", "category": "Food", "amount": "12.40"}]
lines = report_csv(rows).splitlines()
check(lines[1] == "2026-09-02,n/a,Food,12.40", f"unexpected row: {lines[1]!r}")

raw: importer already has its own headings, adjust report_csv for it

hidden.spec: report_csv must not write a header line: its output starts directly with the first data row.
hidden.why: Whether the header should be dropped is not stated; the request only says the importer has its own headings.

from _common import check
from export import report_csv

rows = [{"date": "2026-09-02", "name": "Bakery", "category": "Food", "amount": "12.40"}]

raw: median should always be an amount that was really spent

hidden.spec: median of an even-length list must return the lower of the two middle values: median([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 2 and median([10, 20]) == 10.
hidden.why: Choosing the lower or the upper middle value is arbitrary and the request does not say which.

expect: median returns the lower middle element for even-length lists.
check_source:
from _common import check
from calc import median

check(median([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 2, "median of 1..4 should be 2")
check(median([10, 20]) == 10, "median of 10,20 should be 10")
check(median([5, 1, 3]) == 3, "odd length unchanged")
print("ok")

raw: Food and food are counted as separate categories, merge them

hidden.spec: normalize_category must return the name stripped and lowercased, so ' Food ' becomes 'food' and the report shows one 'food' line (42.50 for rows.csv).
hidden.why: Which spelling the merged category keeps (Food, food or FOOD) is not stated.

expect: normalize_category lowercases names so the report merges Food and food into 'food'.
check_source:
from _common import check, cli
from budget import normalize_category

check(normalize_category(" Food ") == "food", "should be stripped and lowercase")
check(normalize_category("food") == "food", "lowercase stays")
out = cli()
check("  food: 42.50" in out, "merged lowercase line missing")
check("Food:" not in out, "capitalised line should be gone")
print("ok")
